title: Students’ voices on generative AI: perceptions, benefits, and challenges in higher education
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines university students’ perceptions of generative AI (GenAI), especially tools such as ChatGPT, in higher education. The authors aim to understand how familiar students are with GenAI, what benefits and risks they associate with it, and how they think it should be integrated into teaching and learning. The study is motivated by the rapid rise of GenAI and the lack of direct evidence on student perceptions of these tools specifically.

The study used an online survey with both closed-ended and open-ended questions. A total of 399 undergraduate and postgraduate students from six universities in Hong Kong participated. The survey measured knowledge of GenAI, willingness to use it, concerns about its use, and qualitative explanations of perceived benefits and challenges. The context was higher education rather than K-12, and the participants came from a range of disciplines, including STEM and non-STEM fields.

Findings showed generally positive attitudes toward GenAI, with students seeing value in personalized learning support, writing and brainstorming help, research assistance, multimedia creation, and administrative efficiency. At the same time, students expressed concerns about accuracy, transparency, privacy, plagiarism, over-reliance, effects on critical thinking and creativity, career prospects, human values, and unclear policy guidance. The authors conclude that GenAI should be integrated cautiously and responsibly, with attention to AI literacy, ethical use, institutional policy, and support for higher-order skills.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: An OpenAI conversational large language model chatbot that generates human-like text responses and can assist with writing, brainstorming, question answering, summarization, and feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the primary example of generative AI technology in a survey of university students’ familiarity, willingness to use, perceived benefits, and concerns about GenAI in higher education.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a cross-sectional survey with open-ended responses, so it provides perception data but not causal evidence of learning effects. The study is methodologically clear, but it is not an intervention or comparative effectiveness design.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports positive perceptions and perceived utility rather than measured learning outcomes. No effect sizes are reported, and the evidence supports possible usefulness but not demonstrated impact on achievement.
